discovery: Time reversal and wavefront shaping of waves in complex media: turning multiple scattering into a tool for focusing and imaging

nominees.name: Mathias Fink
nominees.affiliation: Institut Langevin, ESPCI Paris - PSL, France

subfield: Wave physics / optics of complex media
motivation: For a century, multiple scattering was treated as the enemy of imaging. Mathias Fink showed with time-reversal mirrors that waves propagating through disordered media can be refocused exactly, and that the disorder itself improves the focus. Ivo Vellekoop and Allard Mosk carried this idea into optics in 2007: by shaping the incident wavefront, they focused coherent light through opaque, strongly scattering layers. This showed that the deterministic, linear nature of scattering can be exploited even in the diffusive regime. Together these works launched the field of wavefront shaping. It brought mesoscopic physics, such as open transmission eigenchannels and transmission matrices, into experiment, and it now underpins deep-tissue and endoscopic imaging, acoustic and seismic focusing, optical computing and high-dimensional quantum optics. The discovery turns disorder from a fundamental limitation into a resource, and its conceptual reach extends across all of wave physics.
